transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-11
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Jacob Miller (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Marcus Lee (Redwood CSM), Elena Ortiz (Cormorant Head of Security), Ravi Patel (Procurement), Samir Khan (Platform Lead), Laura Chen (Legal)

Summary:
Quick procurement/contract review to align on MSA/DPA redlines, SLAs for dedicated vs hosted, pricing approvals process, and next steps for vendor onboarding and technical benchmark for private deployment.

Topics:
- MSA & DPA redlines and timeline
- SLA targets and remedies for Dedicated vs Hosted API
- Data residency, encryption, KMS, audit logs
- SSO/SAML and RBAC for onboarding
- Pricing approval path and PO timing
- Technical benchmark for private deployment

Transcript:
[00:00] Jacob Miller: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call, we got Cormorant and Redwood on — I see Elena, Ravi, Samir and Laura, hey team.
[00:07] Elena Ortiz: Hi Jacob, thanks.
[00:09] Ravi Patel: Hi all.
[00:11] Priya Shah: Priya here from Redwood, will cover technical bits.
[00:14] Marcus Lee: Marcus on CSM, here to help with onboarding timeline.
[00:18] Laura Chen: Laura from legal.
[00:20] Samir Khan: Samir, Platform.
[00:22] Jacob Miller: Great. Purpose today is procurement and legal alignment — MSA, DPA, any SLA asks, and we can also talk through private deployment checklist since Samir mentioned compliance constraints.
[00:34] Ravi Patel: For procurement, we need to make sure pricing and billing terms match our PO cycle. We'll likely do annual commitment if legal and security boxes are checked. Usual 60 to 90 day internal approval.
[00:45] Jacob Miller: Understood. Pricing we showed in the previous deck — tiered committed capacity for Dedicated, and pay-as-you-go for Hosted. We can include a PO-friendly invoice schedule.
[00:53] Laura Chen: On the MSA/DPA, we had three main asks: stronger limitation of liability caps, specific data residency language for EU data, and clearer breach notification timelines. Also need to confirm encryption at rest and KMS options.
[01:09] Priya Shah: On the encryption and KMS piece, Redwood supports customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM for Private and Dedicated options, and for Hosted we offer envelope encryption with Redwood-managed KMS but can discuss bringing-your-own in enterprise plans.
[01:27] Elena Ortiz: Can you clarify the audit logs and retention? We need an immutable audit trail for 12 months and ability to export logs to our SIEM.
[01:36] Priya Shah: We provide per-request audit logs, and for Dedicated/Private we can configure log shipping to a customer-owned endpoint, S3 or syslog. Retention is configurable; default is 90 days but enterprise packages can be extended to 12 months.
[01:51] Samir Khan: Important: our security team will want to run a pen test or at least ask for results, and SOC 2 Type II is a must. Do you have ISO or industry certs?
[02:02] Jacob Miller: Yes, Redwood is SOC 2 Type II and we are pursuing ISO 27001; we'll surface cert artifacts. We can also share a pen test report under NDA.
[02:12] Laura Chen: Liability cap discussion — our legal prefers a tiered cap tied to fees paid in the prior 12 months, and explicit carveouts for intentional breaches.
[02:23] Jacob Miller: We can be flexible on that; typical Redwood language is limited to fees paid, but we can discuss proportional caps for strategic deals. I'll flag that to our legal.
[02:32] Ravi Patel: Timeline wise, procurement needs the redlined MSA/DPA to route for exec approval. Can you commit to a date?
[02:39] Jacob Miller: Yes, we can get redlines over by next Wednesday — March 18th.
[02:43] Laura Chen: Good. For the DPA, are you able to add data processing addendum clauses for EU data transfers? Standard SCCs are needed if you process EU personal data.
[02:54] Priya Shah: We support SCCs and can add EU data residency options on Private or Dedicated. Hosted can be region-restricted as well but for full residency we recommend Dedicated or Private.
[03:06] Elena Ortiz: On the SLA side, what's the SLA for latency and uptime, and what remedies are offered? We need 99.9% uptime for critical endpoints and a credit structure.
[03:16] Jacob Miller: For Hosted API typical SLA is 99.95% availability for paid tiers. Dedicated comes with SLA commitments we can tailor — 99.9 to 99.99 depending on the reserved capacity. Remedies are service credits; we can discuss a nominal cap.
[03:29] Samir Khan: If we go Private on-prem, the availability SLA is on us for infra, but Redwood will commit to support SLAs and response times. Also curious about model fallbacks and graceful degradation — if we lose capacity in a region, how do you route?
[03:43] Priya Shah: Smart routing can failover to a secondary region or to a compatible model variant with a different performance profile. For Private it will be dependent on the customer's infra; we provide the orchestrator but don't maintain the VMs in that case.
[03:56] Ravi Patel: Pricing question — what is the commitment threshold for Dedicated to get the discounted unit rates?
[04:01] Jacob Miller: Typically starts around a 6-12 month committed spend for discounted pricing; examples in the pricing deck show a 12-month commit for best unit costs. We can tailor.
[04:10] Laura Chen: Indemnity and IP — we need language that our data doesn't become Redwood property; also reverse indemnities for third-party claims.
[04:19] Jacob Miller: Redwood does not claim ownership of customer data. We'll review indemnity language in the redlines.
[04:24] [Brief cross-talk]
[04:30] Elena Ortiz: On SSO and RBAC, can you support SAML and SCIM provisioning? We need group-based role assignment.
[04:36] Priya Shah: Yes, SAML SSO, SCIM for user provisioning, and RBAC with role tiers. For Dedicated/Private we can also integrate with customer IdP and directory.
[04:45] Samir Khan: For private deployment we need a checklist: network topology, firewall rules, egress requirements, KMS integration steps. Can you produce that?
[04:53] Priya Shah: Absolutely — we'll produce a private deployment runbook. I'll include a checklist for port ranges, NAT, egress, and KV cache considerations.
[05:03] Jacob Miller: Next, pricing approvals — Ravi, what's your internal cadence?
[05:07] Ravi Patel: We have a bi-weekly procurement committee; if we have a signed MSA + DPA and pricing on file by the end of month, we can align the PO for April billing.
[05:17] Marcus Lee: On onboarding, we recommend a pilot: 30 days of dedicated evaluation with a small reserved capacity or private sandbox to run benchmarks. That helps with cost vs latency tradeoffs.
[05:28] Samir Khan: For benchmarking, we want to test latency p50/p95 for our typical payloads, and cost per token estimates. Also quantization differences — we run some embeddings heavy tasks.
[05:40] Priya Shah: We can run a benchmark harness; we support continuous batching and KV cache which affects token cost. We'll need sample payloads and sequence length distributions.
[05:50] Elena Ortiz: Also want to confirm retention of logs and export format for audits — CSV or JSON?
[05:56] Priya Shah: Both are supported. We'll include schema for audit events.
[06:02] Laura Chen: On confidentiality and breach notification, can you commit to 72 hour notification for confirmed breaches?
[06:08] Jacob Miller: Standard Redwood timeline is 72 hours for confirmed incidents; we can commit that in the DPA.
[06:14] Ravi Patel: Are there any data residency surcharges for EU hosting?
[06:18] Jacob Miller: There can be a modest premium for dedicated region residency due to capacity planning; we'll include figures in the redlined pricing schedule.
[06:26] Samir Khan: For the private on-prem appliance, is there a supported list of hardware? We run on NVIDIA H100 clusters, but want to know minimal specs.
[06:34] Priya Shah: We'll provide recommended GPU SKUs and memory specs; H100 supported and we also have quantized paths for A100 and lower-cost options.
[06:42] Elena Ortiz: Can Redwood provide a SOC 2 attestation and architecture diagram for our security review?
[06:46] Marcus Lee: Yes, we'll push SOC 2 Type II report and high-level architecture diagrams via a secure link.
[06:51] [Silence / notes]
[06:55] Jacob Miller: Ok let me summarize actions: Redwood sends redlined MSA and DPA and pricing schedule by 2026-03-18; Priya will send private deployment runbook and benchmark checklist by 2026-03-20; Cormorant to provide data residency and retention specifics by 2026-03-17; schedule benchmark week of 2026-03-23. Any objections?
[07:15] Laura Chen: That timeline works for legal to start routing.
[07:18] Ravi Patel: Good from procurement.
[07:20] Elena Ortiz: We'll get the residency details over.
[07:23] Jacob Miller: Great. A couple quick clarifications on SLA remedies — Laura, do you need a specific credit formula?
[07:31] Laura Chen: Yes, a simple credit scheme tied to monthly fees is easiest. We can propose language after seeing the redline.
[07:39] Jacob Miller: Perfect. Competitors we discussed — a note that we can show benchmarks vs Anthropic and OpenAI in hosted comparisons, but private deployment is one of our differentiators.
[07:51] Samir Khan: One more: monitoring and tracing, can we integrate Redwood traces into our Grafana/tempo?
[07:57] Priya Shah: Yes, we have tracing hooks and can forward spans to customer endpoints. We'll include instrumentation docs.
[08:05] Marcus Lee: I'll be the onboarding PM — make sure to CC me on all artifacts.
[08:09] Jacob Miller: Noted, Marcus.
[08:11] Ravi Patel: If we get the redlines by next week, legal and procurement can likely execute by end of month. That helps our Q2 budget.
[08:21] Jacob Miller: Awesome, thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the redlines and the runbook.
[08:25] Laura Chen: Thanks.
[08:26] Elena Ortiz: Thanks all.
[08:28] Priya Shah: Bye.
